comments.note: Zip-Slip guard uses Path.GetFullPath + prefix comparison with StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase. This is correct on case-insensitive filesystems (Windows) but could miss case-sensitive traversal on Linux. Since the tool primarily targets Windows (zip = Windows builds per the plan), this is acceptable but worth noting for a future Linux port.

Directory entries (entries with no Name / trailing slash) are skipped explicitly. This is correct behaviour but not tested. A test case confirming directory-only entries don't produce empty files would improve coverage.

TempDirectory was duplicated from VideoIndexer.Tests.Fixtures into VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests.Fixtures because cross-test-project references are undesirable. If a third test project needs it, a shared test helpers assembly should be considered.

summary: Reviewed 3 files (ZipArchiveExtractor.cs, ZipArchiveExtractorTests.cs, TempDirectory.cs). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 3 Low, 0 Info. Zip-Slip guard verified correct and robust against UNC/absolute-path bypass. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Zip-Slip guard reviewed: (1) canonicalizes destination with Path.GetFullPath, (2) appends trailing separator to prevent adjacent-directory prefix collisions, (3) canonicalizes each entry's resolved path. UNC-path bypass tested: Path.Combine with an absolute second argument returns the second argument, but resulting path still fails StartsWith check — not escapable. Guard is correct and complete for Windows/case-insensitive deployments.

[Low] A03 — OrdinalIgnoreCase on case-sensitive Linux FS: Zip-Slip guard uses StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase. On Linux ext4/btrfs (case-sensitive), a destination path and resolved entry path that differ only in casing of the destination prefix could produce a false-positive allow. This does not introduce a true Zip-Slip escape; the check still rejects traversal into different directories. Windows-primary deployment mitigates this. Remediation: if Linux support is added, switch to StringComparison.Ordinal and ensure paths are constructed with consistent casing.

[Low] A04 — No zip bomb protection: no check on ZipArchiveEntry.Length (uncompressed size) or entry count before extraction begins. A crafted archive with extreme compression ratio could exhaust disk space. Risk is Low given the zip is downloaded from a trusted, application-configured URL (ffmpeg official releases) and written to an application-controlled temp directory. Remediation: add a size check (e.g., reject entries with Length > 2 GB) for defense-in-depth.

[Low] A04 — Partial extraction not rolled back on cancellation: ThrowIfCancellationRequested is called per-entry loop iteration but already-extracted files are not cleaned up when cancellation fires mid-archive. File: ZipArchiveExtractor.cs, line 38. Not a security vulnerability but callers must manage destination directory cleanup on OperationCanceledException. Remediation: document this caller responsibility in the IArchiveExtractor interface XML doc.

No Critical or High findings. Zip-Slip protection is correctly implemented using the standard Path.GetFullPath + trailing-separator + StartsWith pattern. CancellationToken checked at start of each loop iteration. FileShare.None on output stream.

summary: Code review passed. ZipArchiveExtractor is clean and security-conscious: correct Zip-Slip guard (Path.GetFullPath + trailing separator), per-entry cancellation check, idiomatic async streams with await using, Directory.CreateDirectory idempotent. Tests cover flat, nested, traversal-throws, and traversal-leaves-no-files-outside-dest. One documentation-forward recorded for IArchiveExtractor interface exception tags.

comments.note: [documentation-forward] IArchiveExtractor.ExtractAsync interface method is missing <exception cref='InvalidDataException'> and <exception cref='OperationCanceledException'> XML doc tags. These are documented on the implementation via inheritdoc extension but should be declared on the interface contract directly.

Zip-Slip guard implementation is textbook correct: Path.GetFullPath canonicalization + trailing separator ensures that a dest of '/tmp/out' cannot be escaped by entries resolving to '/tmp/output_evil'. CancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested at the top of each iteration is the right placement. Directory.CreateDirectory is idempotent. await using on both entry and file streams is correct.
